_comment: OASIS offline package manifest — the single source of truth for every
external package / driver / library OASIS installs. Two consumers:
• the BUILDER (scripts/create-oasis-offline.py) vendors these into the
offline bundle, per suite + per arch, and writes resolved versions back
reads it on the Pi to decide source (newest of apt vs bundle vs installed),
enforce `min_version` capability gates, then install/test/create services.
Source `type`: apt | github-release | pypi | url | data.
Suite-aware on purpose: a single-suite bundle installed librtlsdr 0.6.0
(bookworm) on a Trixie host, which lacks RTL-SDR Blog V4 support (needs >= 2.0).

server.description: Flask web server + WSGI + system stats. Vendored as wheels per platform/python.

rtl-sdr.description: RTL-SDR RX driver + userspace tools (rtl_fm, rtl_test).

librtlsdr.reason: RTL-SDR Blog V4 (R828D) support requires librtlsdr/rtl-sdr >= 2.0. Bookworm ships pre-2.0 and breaks the V4.

rtl-sdr-feed.description: Carries/verifies the RTL-SDR -> GrayWolf sdr_udp audio feed. socat (feed) + tcpdump (verify) and their not-always-present shared-lib deps.

rtl-sdr-diag.description: Standalone AFSK1200 decoder for bench-testing the SDR chain independently of GrayWolf.
rtl-sdr-diag._note: Pulls a larger X11/audio dependency tree than the feed tools; only multimon-ng itself is vendored, so its deps may resolve from apt on a minimal image. Diagnostic only — not required for the GrayWolf feed.

rtl-sdr-bench.description: Interactive SDR tuning-bench decoder deps: sox (scales audio into Direwolf's demod range) for features/rtl-sdr/tune-rtl-sdr.py. Direwolf itself is vendored under the 'direwolf' bundle group; only sox is added here.
rtl-sdr-bench._note: sox is small and universally present in apt; vendored best-effort so a fully-offline install still gets it. Its `resolved` versions are populated by scripts/create-oasis-offline.py on the connected build machine.

graywolf.description: GrayWolf APRS TNC / iGate / digipeater. Prebuilt .deb per arch from GitHub releases.
graywolf._note: Upstream ships only arm64 and amd64 .deb assets — no armhf.

kiwix.description: kiwix-serve offline content server. Prebuilt static tarball per arch.

webssh.description: ttyd browser SSH terminal. Prebuilt static binary per arch from GitHub releases.

winlink.description: Pat Winlink client + web UI (store-and-forward email over radio).

direwolf.description: Direwolf AX.25 packet modem — the RF (packet) transport behind Pat's AGWPE. Started on demand (hardware-exclusive with GrayWolf); see docs/plan-winlink.md.
direwolf._note: The bundler downloads only the packages named below (no dep-closure resolution). Direwolf's runtime deps (libhamlib*, libgps*, libasound2* — names differ bookworm vs trixie under the t64 transition) must be added to by_suite when bundling on the connected build machine, so the fully-offline `apt install ./*.deb` resolves. Most are already on a stock Pi OS image; libhamlib is the one to be sure of.

dump1090-fa.description: dump1090-fa Mode S/ADS-B decoder — owns the RTL-SDR and writes live aircraft positions consumed by services/adsb's adsb-api. Off by default; started on demand from the dashboard's ADS-B card (mutually exclusive with other RTL-SDR features, e.g. GrayWolf).
dump1090-fa._note: dump1090-fa is distributed by FlightAware, not the base Debian/Raspberry Pi OS apt repos. create-oasis-offline.py now vendors dump1090-fa per suite/arch directly from FlightAware package indexes into services/adsb/packages/dump1090-fa/<suite>/. Runtime dependencies may still vary by target image, so keep online fallback available when dependency closure is incomplete.

openwebrx.description: OpenWebRX+ — browser-based, receive-only SDR receiver/decoder (SIGINT/monitoring) on :8073. Installed online from the OpenWebRX+ upstream apt repo (third-party); NOT vendored into the offline bundle. Off by default (exclusive RTL-SDR use; start from the dashboard).

satellites-voice.description: Text-to-speech stack for the Satellites page's spoken pass alert — speech-dispatcher + espeak-ng, so Chromium's Web Speech API exposes a voice. Optional: without it, pass alerts still chime. The installer is offline-first (bundled .debs, else apt) and no-ops off-Linux.
satellites-voice._note: The bundler downloads only the packages named below (no dep-closure resolution). speech-dispatcher's runtime deps (libspeechd2, libsonic0, libdotconf0, and the espeak-ng data/libs — names can differ bookworm vs trixie under the t64 transition) must be curated into by_suite when bundling on the connected build machine, so a fully-offline `apt install ./*.deb` resolves. Several are already on a stock Pi OS Desktop image.

satellites.description: Satellite pass-prediction Python stack (services/satellites/predict.py) — Skyfield over the SGP4 propagator plus its compiled numpy dependency. Shares the server wheel set (server/wheels/, bundled from scripts/requirements.txt). Installed into the venv by services/satellites/install-predict.py when the Satellites feature is set up; without it the roster still loads but /api/satellites/passes and /track 500 (no prediction engine).
satellites._note: Version ranges (not exact pins) for the compiled wheels so pip picks the right per-interpreter build offline, matching scripts/requirements.txt: numpy ships 2.0.2 (py3.9) / 2.2.6 (py3.10-3.13) / 2.5.1 (py3.14) and sgp4 2.25 (cp39/cp310) / 2.27 (cp311-abi3). Skyfield is a pure none-any wheel (pinned exactly) and pulls jplephem + certifi transitively from the same wheel dir.

ai.description: AI assistant Python stack (ai/): the MCP SDK + httpx client. Shares the server wheel set (server/wheels/, bundled from scripts/requirements.txt). Installed into the venv by ai/runtime/install.py when the AI assistant feature is set up. Without it the assistant blueprint still imports (lazy) but /api/assistant/* returns errors.
ai._note: mcp requires Python >=3.10 (so does anyio); the AI feature is gated to Pi 5 / 8 GB which runs Bookworm (3.11) or Trixie (3.13). Both mcp and httpx are pure none-any wheels. The base server install on a 3.9 box must NOT install these — they belong to this feature group only.

ai-llama.description: llama.cpp llama-server (prebuilt Ubuntu arm64). The OpenAI-compatible local-model endpoint for the AI assistant, run as the oasis-ai systemd daemon. Ubuntu-built — confirmed on Pi OS (Debian) arm64 during Pi verification.

ai-model.description: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct GGUF (Q4_K_M), the default assistant model. ~1.9 GB, single file. Vendored into the offline bundle (offline-packages/ai-model/) by phase_ai so the ai feature installs fully offline; ai/runtime/install.py copies it to ai/models/ (gitignored). Swappable via ai/config.json.

pmtiles.description: Protomaps go-pmtiles CLI. Converts MBTiles -> PMTiles offline (used by maps/convert-mbtiles.py). Vendored into the bundle's maps/ directory. By default only the Linux binaries (the bundle's Pi/Linux targets) are fetched; macOS/Windows platforms are marked default=false and included only with create-oasis-offline.py --all-platforms so the default bundle stays lean.

fcc.description: FCC amateur license database (EN.dat/HD.dat) + ZIP-to-grid table. Large one-time download, not vendored in the bundle.

wikipedia.description: Wikipedia ZIM snapshot for Kiwix. Large one-time download (1 GB - 100 GB), not vendored in the bundle.

ap-fallback.description: Wi-Fi AP fallback + dashboard Wi-Fi picker (scripts/enable-ap-fallback.py). NetworkManager drives the OASIS WPA2 hotspot; avahi-daemon resolves oasis.local. Both ship in the Raspberry Pi OS base image, so on a standard install this is a no-op; listed so a minimal image can vendor them.
